title: Airstream Condition Sorter
description: Ten shuffled application descriptions tagged with every airstream condition they present (hot, wet, corrosive, particulate-laden, explosive atmosphere) or Clean; exact-set scoring with feedback naming missing and extra tags, and an end list of missed items.
creator: Twin City Fan
subject: airstream
hot airstream
wet airstream
corrosive airstream
particulate-laden airstream
explosive atmosphere
rights: Copyright 2026 Twin City Fan. All rights reserved.

educational.audience: Adult professional development: new application engineers, sales staff, representatives and facilities staff
educational.topic: Recognizing airstream conditions on a fan inquiry
learningObjectives: The learner will classify ten application descriptions by every airstream condition they present (hot, wet, corrosive, particulate-laden, explosive atmosphere, or clean), matching the answer key on at least 8 of 10.

accessibility.notes: describe() text (fallback mode); tags are aria-pressed toggle buttons with a ✓ prefix and heavier outline when selected; each ⓘ button has an aria-label; selections, verdicts, definitions and the summary announced through FP.announce (aria-live); ✓/✗ glyphs and solid/dashed borders pair with colour; keys 1-6 toggle tags, Enter submits and goes to the next item.

controls.label: Hot / Wet / Corrosive / Particulate-laden / Explosive atmosphere / Clean

controls.purpose: Show the definition of the tag beside it

controls.label: Start over
controls.purpose: New shuffle; later runs are practice

rules: Tags are multi-select; Clean clears all other tags and any other tag clears Clean
An empty selection cannot be submitted
Correct means an exact set match with the key; one attempt per item
Items shown in shuffled order; only the first run counts as evidence
assumptions: Descriptions are illustrative applications; temperature judgments rest on FanPedia pp. 110-116 as summarized in Chapter 2
limitations: Real inquiries need the material, chemical or hazard named, not just the condition

sources: Tag definitions: Chapter 2, 'The Airstreams Fans Handle'
High-temperature package ranges: FanPedia pp. 110-116, as summarized in Chapter 2
Item descriptions: illustrative applications written for this sim

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Multi-select classification with immediate per-item feedback naming missing and extra tags
keyQuestions: Which applications combine two conditions, and why?
When is warm air not a hot airstream?
Why is grain dust both particulate-laden and an explosive atmosphere?
commonMisconceptions: Each airstream has only one condition
Combustible dust is only a particulate problem
Any chemical exhaust is an explosive atmosphere
assessmentOpportunities: End score shown as 'Score: n of 10' (running line 'Items correct: n of 10'); mastery is 8 of 10 on the first run.
